title: What If Every Moth on Earth Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if every moth vanished tonight? Your garden wouldn't notice at dusk. It would by midnight.
Moths are the night shift. Scientists swabbed 838 of them, and nearly half, 45 percent, carried pollen.
That pollen came from 47 plant species, including at least seven that bees, hoverflies and butterflies rarely visit.
Those plants would lose a pollinator nothing else replaces. Fewer flowers might set seed, and fewer seeds means fewer plants.
How much our crops depend on moths? Researchers say nobody knows yet. Nobody has fully checked.
And moths are already in steep decline across the globe. The experiment is running. We just aren't watching the night shift.
